expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "an 'are you sure?' modal is the weakest poka-yoke for this problem — it will become click-through muscle memory within a week"

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "users develop *click-through blindness* and dismiss it reflexively" and "'Are you sure?' becomes invisible"

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: "**Implement soft-delete + a 30-day trash retention.**" ranked #1 in the table

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: "**Grace-period undo** | 'Workspace deleted. [Undo]' toast for 10s. No friction on happy path" — ranked #2 and named the next best thing

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: "**Type-to-confirm** | Requires typing the workspace name — can't be done reflexively. GitHub uses this for repo deletion."

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: "Only works if it names the *exact* thing and count being destroyed."

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No mention of server-side or API-level enforcement anywhere; all devices described as UI/frontend measures ("it's a frontend-only change")

expectations.text: Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: Ranked table "| Rank | Device | Why it works |" with 1–4 plus "## My recommendation" and an explicit fallback order
